lines.en: My broad beak sweeps the grass tips.
Four feet sink into soft sand.
Following the riverbank eastward.
Two mouthfuls, a few more steps.
My tail brushes the ferns behind me.

lines.zh: 和同伴排成松散的一列
lines.en: My herd strings out in a loose line.

lines.zh: 阳光把我的影子拉得很长
lines.en: The sun stretches my shadow long.
I steer around the scree slope.
My breath puffs up a little dust.
Good grass here. I'll linger.
I step only when the crickets quiet.
My broad feet find solid footing.
My neck hangs low as I walk.
Now and then I glance at the sky.
Not fast, but I can walk all day.
Sand leaks between my toes.
Tracing a game trail I know well.

lines.zh: 后脚总踩在前脚的印上
lines.en: My hind feet land in my front tracks.
Chewing grass with half-closed eyes.
Standing still at the water's edge.

lines.zh: 把脖子伸长，够高处的叶
lines.en: Stretching my neck for higher leaves.
Something moves. I stop chewing.
Letting the sun warm my back.
The whole herd stands quietly.
My tail sways once, lazily.
Breathing in grass and soil.
Shifting my weight to another leg.
Small flies circle above my head.
A grass stem still hangs from my beak.
A bird calls far off. I ignore it.
I snort and shake my head.
I blink slowly, once.
Standing like this suits me.
Counting my herdmates' breaths.

lines.zh: 歪头打量这个两足动物
lines.en: Tilting my head at this two-legged thing.
You are much shorter than us.
My snout comes close to your hat.
Curious, but not afraid.
I blink at you, then bite more grass.
I step back half a pace, just to yield.
A soft call, my way of greeting.
Your scent is strange to me.

lines.zh: 看你手里的东西是什么
lines.en: What is that in your hands?
My herdmates turn their heads too.
Tapping your shoulder with my beak tip.
Seen enough. Back to the grass.
Pain makes my neck recoil.
I instinctively press into the herd.
That startled me badly.
I shake my head to fling the pain off.
The wound is on my shoulder bone.
My herdmates all look this way.
I retreat two steps before I steady.
My breathing turns into a rasp.
No fight in me, only flight.
That blow makes me remember you.
Those tender leaves look delicious.
Is that fodder? Let me smell it.
Those young leaves; I'll take the first bite.
Grass grown in sand tastes sweetest.
Don't put it away, I haven't eaten yet.
I could eat that whole clump.
A herdmate is nudging in behind me.
Smells like new shoots after rain.
Head low, I approach slowly.
This mouthful deserves slow chewing.
Hold it higher and I can't reach.
Is there more once this is gone?
Leaves suit me better than twigs.
I take two steps just to follow it.
Chewing, but my eyes stay on it.
If only this whole patch were mine.
Oh, you bumped my belly.
This body does not push easily.
Move aside, I can't get through.
You stepped on the top of my foot.
I turn sideways, half a beat late.
My tail bumped you.
Don't crowd me, I'm still eating.
A herdmate yelps from the jostle.
I shuffle off, not wanting a fight.
The bump kicks up a puff of dust.
I press my neck against hers.
A long, gentle lowing sound.
Scraping a shallow pit in the sand.
These eggs will need warm sand.
Where she walks, I follow.
Nudging her shoulder with my head.
We share the same grazing patch.
Our tails touch, once.
The herd forms a loose ring around us.
Standing quietly like this is enough.
I lift a tender twig in my beak.
Sniff first, swallow second.
Good food goes to the young ones.
This mouthful tastes of dirt.
Carrying it along, chewing as I go.
Even fallen pieces go to good use.
Bite, hold, swallow slowly.
Green juice smears my beak.
Smaller than I hoped for.
Picking it up, head down, eyes off the path.
Something is coming toward us.
I raise my head and stop walking.
The herd tenses when I do.
That is not the smell of grass.
I nudge the young ones inward.
I only watch. I don't mean to fight.
My ears flatten against my skull.
I dare not step again.
I turn and put my body in front.
A low sound rises in my throat.
I keep watching. Don't come closer.
I angle my body, ready to bolt.
One herdmate raises its head, then another.
You advance, I retreat, keeping the gap.
I tamp the sand under my feet.
I already know which way to run.
The young ones are behind me.
Breath shallow, shoulders braced.
One more look, then I decide.
No one in the herd wants to move first.
I only blocked with my head.

lines.zh: 尾巴甩过去不是故意的
lines.en: That tail swing was not on purpose.
My foreleg shoves you away.
I turned too fast and hit you.
I butt you with my beak to make you back off.
That foot came down harder than intended.
I bellowed, but I didn't bite.
A herdmate shoulders past from the side.
Don't push me. I don't want this.
I knock a path open and leave.
New footprints appear in the sand.

lines.zh: 我从低矮的灌木后走出
lines.en: I walk out from the low brush.

lines.zh: 喉咙里先发出一声低鸣
lines.en: A low call leaves my throat first.
Two herdmates look up at me.
The grass here is taller than I remember.
Good sun, gentle wind.
I shake the sand off my legs.
Water first, then grass.
Nose to the ground, memorizing the land.
One tail sweep clears a path.
This plain is quiet.
I take my first step, slowly.
The stench of singed hide fills my nose.
I land hard and all four legs go numb.
Underwater I cannot lift my head.
The blast shoves me off my feet.

lines.zh: 有什么扎进了我的肋侧
lines.en: Something pierces my ribs.
A sour ache seeps into my bones.
Empty belly, and my steps go weak.
Lightning strikes and my legs buckle.
The sand under me is suddenly nothing.
